data.one_liner: Simplify widget tree structures using extension methods inspired by CSS and SwiftUI.
data.what_it_does: styled_widget uses Dart extension methods to provide a bottom-up, chaining approach for building Flutter widget trees. It lets you apply padding, decoration, layout constraints, alignments, and animations directly to widgets or lists of widgets without deeply nesting widget boilerplate.
use_when: You want a flatter, more readable widget hierarchy using method chaining.
You prefer a bottom-up styling approach similar to CSS or SwiftUI.
avoid_when: Your team prefers traditional nested Flutter widget trees or widget-based composition.
You require complex state management solutions built into the UI kit.
strengths: Drastically reduces boilerplate indentation in widget trees.
Integrates seamlessly with existing Flutter codebases via Dart extension methods.
weaknesses: Method chaining can sometimes obscure standard Flutter debugging or widget inspector flows.
API learning curve for developers accustomed to traditional declarative widgets.
data.minimal_example:
Icon(OMIcons.home, color: Colors.white)
  .padding(all: 10)
  .decorated(color: Color(0xff7AC1E7), shape: BoxShape.circle)
  .alignment(Alignment.center);
